title: Surge depletion: scaling regression triage, emergency ballast, and policy tuning
creator: Aisha Patel
description: During a customer-driven surge on 2025-02-17 several dedicated pools experienced an unexpected headroom drain and autoscaler regressions: scale-outs were delayed, containers entered L7 throttling, and prefix/KV cache hits fell sharply. This ticket coordinates triage, emergency containment ("ballast" capacity and throttles), a rollback to the previous autoscaler policy, and a set of long-term fixes to prevent recurrence. The goal is to restore predictable throughput guarantees for Dedicated customers within the SLA window and implement policy changes that are safe for rollout.
impact_summary: Multiple Dedicated customers observed 30-60% throughput reduction for 15-90 minutes during peak. Latency SLOs were violated for low-latency tier customers; billing exposure and potential SLA credits are possible for impacted accounts.
reproduction_steps: 1) Simulate sustained token-per-second load from 100 synthetic clients pinned to a dedicated pool configuration (n1-highgpu) with mixed short/long sequences
2) Apply current autoscaler policy (policy v3.4) and observe scale decision latency and scale delta limits
3) Introduce 15% artificial KV cache miss rate to emulate cache churn seen in logs
4) Watch horizontal scale decisions, container scheduling delays, and headroom metric (available_rps) in the dedicated-pool dashboard
5) Confirm regression by comparing to a control run using autoscaler policy v3.1 (previous known-good).

root_cause: A confluence of changes caused the regression: 1) autoscaler policy v3.4 introduced a conservative scale delta limiter to prevent thrashing which, under sustained surge, prevented adequate scale-outs; 2) a recent runtime kernel selection optimization reduced eviction priority for low-memory pods, increasing scheduling wobble; and 3) PVC-backed logging introduced transient I/O delays that amplified kube-scheduler latency. Individually each change was low-risk; their interaction under surge load produced the headroom collapse.
mitigation_taken: Applied emergency ballast (reserve nodes) to affected region and routed non-critical customers to burst pool
Rolled back autoscaler policy to v3.1 across affected DCs (see rollback PR)
Temporary route-level circuit breakers to shed best-effort traffic and preserve SLA tiers
Increased KV cache retention for high-throughput routes to reduce cache churn
long_term_actions: Autoscaler: Add surge-mode path that overrides conservative delta limits when headroom trend indicates sustained demand (owner: Marco Chen, due: 2025-03-12)
Scheduler: Re-evaluate kernel priority patch and add canary tests for pod eviction behavior during scheduling spikes (owner: Elena Rivera, due: 2025-03-19)
Storage: Audit PVC mount patterns for logging; implement async buffering to remove critical path I/O from scheduling (owner: Priya Nair, due: 2025-04-02)
